enonce_markdown: Which of the following best describes a project?

choix.texte: A temporary set of planned activities with a start and an end, carried out to produce a unique result
A routine activity repeated every day in an organisation
Any task that is carried out by a computer
A permanent department of a company with no deadline

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A project is temporary (definite start and end), has a specific objective and a unique result, and uses limited time, money and resources. Day-to-day operations are not projects.

### Solution

Installing a network in a school is a project: it has a start, an end and a unique result. Daily operations and permanent departments are ongoing, not temporary, and the use of a computer does not make a task a project.

**Answer: A.**

enonce_markdown:
(a) Define the critical path of a project. (2 marks)

(b) Explain why the project manager must watch the tasks on the critical path more closely than the others. (2 marks)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The critical path is the longest chain of dependent tasks from start to finish; it fixes the minimum duration of the whole project.

### Solution

**(a)** The critical path is the **longest sequence of dependent tasks** from the start to the end of the project. It determines the shortest time in which the project can be completed, and its tasks have zero slack (float).

**(b)** Any delay on a critical task delays the completion date of the whole project, since there is no spare time. Tasks that are not critical have slack and can be delayed up to that time without affecting the end date, so the manager concentrates resources and control on the critical tasks.

enonce_markdown:
A project has the following tasks.

| Task | Duration (days) | Predecessor(s) |
|---|---|---|
| A | 3 | none |
| B | 4 | A |
| C | 7 | A |
| D | 2 | B |
| E | 3 | C, D |
| F | 2 | E |

What is the minimum time in which the project can be completed?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

The minimum duration of a project is the length of its longest path, found by adding the durations along every path from start to finish (forward pass).

### Solution

Paths (checked by script): A-B-D-E-F = 3 + 4 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 14 days; A-C-E-F = 3 + 7 + 3 + 2 = **15 days**. The longest path is the critical path, so the minimum duration is 15 days. 14 days is the length of the other path, 19 days is the sum of A, B, C, E and F (task D ignored but both B and C counted, though they run at the same time), and 21 days is the sum of all durations, which ignores that tasks can run in parallel.

**Answer: C.**

enonce_markdown:
A project has the following tasks.

| Task | Duration (days) | Predecessor(s) |
|---|---|---|
| P | 2 | none |
| Q | 5 | P |
| R | 3 | P |
| S | 4 | Q, R |

What is the slack (float) of task R?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Slack of a task = latest start - earliest start. It is the time by which the task can be delayed without delaying the project.

### Solution

Path P-Q-S = 2 + 5 + 4 = 11 days (critical); path P-R-S = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 days. R can start at day 2 at the earliest, and must finish by day 7 when S starts, so its latest start is 7 - 3 = 4. Slack = 4 - 2 = **2 days** (checked by script), which is also 11 - 9. 0 is the slack of a critical task, 3 is the duration of R, not its slack.

**Answer: B.**

enonce_markdown: In a project, task K is not on the critical path and has a slack of 3 days. Because of a supplier's delay, task K finishes 2 days later than planned. What is the effect on the completion date of the project?

choix.texte: The project is delayed by 2 days
The project is delayed by 3 days
The project is delayed by 5 days
No effect, because the delay is smaller than the slack

corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A delay on a non-critical task affects the end date only by the amount exceeding its slack: delay on the project = max(0, task delay - slack).

### Solution

The delay (2 days) is less than the slack (3 days), so the project end date is unchanged: max(0, 2 - 3) = 0. The slack is reduced to 1 day, so the task becomes closer to critical. The other options assume that every delay is passed on to the whole project, which is only true for critical tasks.

**Answer: D.**

enonce_markdown:
A school plans to install a computer network. The tasks of the project are:

| Task | Description | Duration (days) | Predecessor(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Site survey | 4 | none |
| B | Purchase of equipment | 6 | A |
| C | Cable installation | 8 | A |
| D | Server configuration | 5 | B |
| E | Staff training | 3 | D |
| F | Testing and handover | 2 | C, E |

(a) Find the critical path and the minimum duration of the project. (3 marks)

(b) Calculate the slack of task C. (2 marks)

(c) The project team costs 45 000 FCFA per day for the whole duration of the project, and the equipment costs 2 350 000 FCFA. The manager adds a contingency of 10 percent of these two costs. Calculate the total budget. (3 marks)

(d) Task D takes 8 days instead of 5. State the new duration of the project and explain. (2 marks)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Find every path through the network and add its durations: the longest is critical. Slack = critical length - length of the path containing the task. A budget adds the costs and then a percentage for contingency.

### Solution

**(a)** Paths (checked by script): A-B-D-E-F = 4 + 6 + 5 + 3 + 2 = **20 days**; A-C-F = 4 + 8 + 2 = 14 days. The critical path is **A-B-D-E-F** and the minimum duration is **20 days**.

**(b)** C is on the path of 14 days, so its slack is 20 - 14 = **6 days**.

**(c)** Team cost = 45 000 x 20 = 900 000 FCFA. Cost before contingency = 900 000 + 2 350 000 = 3 250 000 FCFA. Contingency = 10 % x 3 250 000 = 325 000 FCFA. Total budget = **3 575 000 FCFA**.

**(d)** D is a critical task with zero slack, so its delay is passed on in full: the critical path becomes 4 + 6 + 8 + 3 + 2 = **23 days** (3 days longer). The path A-C-F is still not critical.
